content.title: About
content.content: Squid are marine cephalopod mollusks widely used in cooking. Frozen in tube form, they are convenient for quick preparation: simply thaw and sauté or boil. Squid have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a firm yet tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Squid belong to the class Cephalopoda, which also includes octopuses and cuttlefish.
The tubes are created by removing the internal organs and cutting the body into rings.
In the wild, squid can change skin colour thanks to chromatophores.
Squid can achieve rapid bursts of speed by jet propulsion, expelling water from a mantle cavity.
Many squid species are bioluminescent, although commercial varieties are usually non‑glowing.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Squid provide about 15–18 g of protein per 100 g, making them an excellent source of high‑quality protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafoods, squid contain very little saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Squid contain vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and riboflavin (B2), important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They are a source of selenium, zinc, copper and iodine, which support thyroid function and antioxidant defenses.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than fatty fish, squid still provide EPA and DHA, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to squid, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Squid are high in purines, so people with gout should limit their intake.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Like other marine products, squid can contain traces of heavy metals; purchase from reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen squid tubes are easy to cook in a skillet, wok, or boiled in broth for 3–5 minutes. They can be added to pasta, risotto, salads, soups, and seafood mixes. For best results, quickly thaw in the refrigerator or under running water before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen squid at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Discard any product with off‑odors or discoloration.
